candidate_overrides.source_notes: Official Japan Coast Guard page says Abashiri began on 1950-06-01 as Kushiro Coast Guard Office Abashiri Guard/Rescue Station, later renamed/reassigned.

candidate_overrides.name: Nagoyako Kaijo Kotsu Center

candidate_overrides.name: Shonan Kaijo Hoansho

candidate_overrides.name: Champ de manoeuvre Chilcotin
candidate_overrides.source_notes: French alias for Chilcotin Training Area. DND's 1923 report lists Chilcotin, B.C. Training Area land acquired from British Columbia; BC Geographical Names ties Champ de manoeuvre Chilcotin/Canadian Forces Camp Chilcotin to the official Chilcotin Training Area; CanadaBuys/DND material says the area is DND-owned and used as a military training area.

candidate_overrides.name: Chilcotin Training Area
candidate_overrides.source_notes: DND's 1923 report lists Chilcotin, B.C. Training Area land acquired from British Columbia; BC Geographical Names confirms the official training-area identity and later naming history; CanadaBuys/DND material documents current DND ownership/use as a military training area. Use 1923 as acquisition/use floor, not a construction date.

candidate_overrides.name: Champ de manoeuvre Sussex
candidate_overrides.source_notes: GeoNB lists Champ de manoeuvre Sussex as a Canadian Forces Range and/or Training Area. MilitaryBruce states Camp Sussex opened in 1885, the camp closed in 1965, the rifle range continued into the early 1980s, and part of the property/training area continued in DND/CFB Gagetown use. Confidence medium due mixed camp/range continuity.

candidate_overrides.name: Sussex Training Area
candidate_overrides.source_notes: GeoNB lists Sussex Training Area as a Canadian Forces Range and/or Training Area. MilitaryBruce states Camp Sussex opened in 1885, closed in 1965, its rifle range continued into the early 1980s, and the training area continued to be used by troops from CFB Gagetown. Confidence medium due mixed camp/range continuity.
